questions.q: Which four humor types does the summary describe?
a: Stand-ups, magnets, sweethearts and snipers
Clowns, critics, storytellers and mimics
Observers, teasers, jesters and roasters
Pranksters, comics, satirists and wits
questions.why: Lesson 1 names the stand-ups, magnets, sweethearts and snipers.

a: Positive and naturally fun to be around
Dark and expressive like a roast
Sarcastic and aggressive with one-liners
Innocent and careful about timing
questions.why: Lesson 1 says magnets spread positivity and are the ones who make crowds laugh.

questions.q: What is the best basis for humor?
a: The truth of everyday things that happen
Shocking stories about strangers
Clever wordplay without context
Exaggerated claims about coworkers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says people relate most to the truth, so jokes should draw on real life.

questions.q: What does the rule of three involve?
a: Two expected items and a third surprise
Three jokes delivered quickly in a row
Three friends sharing a single story
Repeating the punchline three times
questions.why: Lesson 3 says list two expected things and add a third unexpected element.

questions.q: Why does exaggeration work in a story?
a: It turns the story around unexpectedly
It makes the story longer and more detailed
It proves that the story is true
It hides the point of the joke
questions.why: Lesson 3 says exaggeration works when it takes the listener by surprise.
